intro: Q3 2026 opens with the structural AI thesis confirmed across three independent data points in the past week: Micron Q3 FY26 +15.7% beat (HBM4 sold out), NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra (GB300) achieving 1.5x H100 performance, and Samsung's $226B AI data center commitment. The long-term framework question shifts from 'will AI capex sustain?' to 'who captures the monetization layer?' The July 1 triple-gate test (NVDA, SPX, VIX all simultaneously approaching thresholds) signals that the institutional step-aside from the May 14 ATH may be ending. Long-term theses to establish or reinforce in Q3 2026: AI semiconductor infrastructure (NVDA, MU), AI platform monetization (META, MSFT, GOOGL), crypto risk-on (BTC post-halving cycle), and space infrastructure (SPCX pre-earnings). The FOMC Warsh hawkish hold (3.80% median year-end, cuts to 2027–2028) is the primary discount-rate headwind for long-duration growth assets — but AI revenue confirmation (not multiple expansion) is the driver of the structural theses here.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.idea: NVDA is the dominant structural AI infrastructure pick. The mandatory exit (Stop Day 2, June 29 close $194.97) was a risk-management protocol, not a fundamental thesis change. Blackwell Ultra (GB300 NVL72 = 1.5x GB200 performance) is shipping, sovereign AI capex ($100B+ from EU, Japan, Saudi Arabia, UAE) is confirmed, and the HBM memory supply chain is locked in with SK Hynix/Micron through H2 2026. Q3 Day 1 intraday data shows NVDA touching $200.63 — the $200 gate is being tested. Q2 FY27 earnings (est. late July) with ~$91B quarterly revenue guidance is the structural re-entry confirmation.
ideas.why: Every major AI model training and inference deployment runs on NVIDIA hardware. The switching cost is 18–24 months of software re-optimization — AMD and Intel cannot close this gap in FY27. MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META are all committed to multi-year NVDA GPU purchases. Blackwell's revenue opportunity per AI factory is 50x greater than Hopper — the platform transition creates a structural ASP uplift that will compound through FY26–FY27. The $195 supply overhang is tactical profit-taking, not fundamental deterioration.
ideas.driver: Blackwell B300 GPU ramp (H2 2026) expanding compute density 3x vs H100; sovereign AI capex from EU, Japan, Saudi Arabia, UAE; inference demand scaling faster than training as AI moves from development to deployment; Q2 FY27 earnings confirming >$91B quarterly guide; Rubin architecture roadmap (2026 successor) extending competitive moat
ideas.risk: US export controls tighten restricting H20/B20 sales to China (removes ~$10–15B annual revenue); AMD MI400 achieves competitive performance within 12 months; hyperscaler capex cuts in H1 2027 if AI monetization disappoints investors; FOMC rate hold through 2027 compresses long-duration multiple from current ~35x forward

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: MU is the most compelling near-term AI semi structural buy after Q3 FY26 +15.7% earnings beat. HBM4 sold out through 2026. $50B Q4 FY26 guide (~40% above prior consensus) removes execution uncertainty for the next two quarters. The US domestic manufacturing advantage (Idaho fab) is a geopolitical moat that Samsung and SK Hynix cannot replicate for US government AI procurement. No forced-exit overhang, no ADR mechanics — cleanest technical setup of any AI semi.
ideas.why: Samsung's $226B AI data center commitment validated MU's $50B Q4 guide at national-government scale. The HBM market is a structural oligopoly: three players (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) with pricing discipline enforced by technological complexity. CHIPS Act incentives are reducing MU's per-wafer cost at scale. DoD AI procurement mandates specifically favor US-manufactured HBM. Q4 FY26 earnings in September will set up FY27 at a $200B+ annual revenue run rate.
ideas.driver: HBM4 ramp through H2 2026 — $50B Q4 FY26 guide sets FY27 at $200B+ run rate; CHIPS Act fab incentives reducing Idaho HBM4 production cost; DoD AI procurement mandate for US-manufactured HBM; September Q4 FY26 earnings confirmation of the HBM demand cycle duration; pricing discipline in oligopolistic 3-player HBM market
ideas.risk: HBM demand cycle peaks in H1 2027 earlier than expected as AI model efficiency improvements reduce memory per compute unit; Samsung or SK Hynix aggressive pricing to defend share; China export controls remove HBM export channel; Q4 FY26 guide miss (volume shortfall or ASP compression)

ideas.name: SK Hynix
ideas.timeframe: 3–9 months (through Nasdaq ADR seasoning and Q3 2026 earnings)
ideas.idea: SK Hynix structural thesis: world's largest HBM3e and HBM4 supplier ahead of Nasdaq ADR listing July 10 (SKHY, $29.4B, BofA/Goldman/Citi/JPMorgan). The ADR transforms the investor base from Korean retail + Asian institutional to global institutional — a structural re-rating event. CONVICTION LOWERED TO LOW from MEDIUM: July 1 intraday low ₩2,502,000 breached the ₩2,540,000 mandatory stop; KOSPI Gate 1 failed on Q3 Day 1; close buffer is only ₩44,000. Hold the position through ADR listing if stop is not triggered. Post-ADR: MSCI inclusion drives systematic rebalancing demand for 3–6 months.
ideas.why: SK Hynix supplies HBM3e exclusively to NVIDIA for H100/H200 and is ramping HBM4 for Blackwell B300. The supply relationship gives revenue visibility through H2 2026. Samsung's HBM3E disqualification extends SK Hynix's NVIDIA monopoly through at least H1 2027. The Nasdaq ADR listing is structurally transformative: it opens the US institutional market to Korea's most important AI semiconductor company for the first time with meaningful liquidity.
ideas.driver: July 10 Nasdaq ADR listing (SKHY, $29.4B) — largest Korean Nasdaq listing ever; post-ADR MSCI World index inclusion process; HBM4 ramp as primary NVDA Blackwell supplier; Q3 2026 earnings (August) confirming HBM4 ASP premium over HBM3e; KOSPI ADR-listing-driven institutional reallocation
ideas.risk: July 1 intraday breach of mandatory stop (₩2,502,000 low vs ₩2,540,000 stop) — if July 2 or subsequent KST session closes below ₩2,540,000, mandatory exit triggers; KOSPI macro deterioration; ADR listing supply overhang (17.79M new Nasdaq shares hitting the market July 10); NVDA supply diversification toward Samsung if HBM4 yield improves

ideas.name: Microsoft Corporation
ideas.idea: Microsoft is the most diversified AI monetization play: Azure AI cloud (OpenAI partnership, exclusive enterprise deployment), Copilot productivity suite (365 seats at $30/month premium), GitHub Copilot (developer workflow capture). FOMC hawkish hold through 2027–2028 pressures growth multiples but MSFT's $100B+ FCF generation and ~2% dividend yield provide a rate-resistant floor that pure-growth AI names lack.
ideas.why: Enterprise AI adoption in 2026 is about Copilot seat expansion, not new product launches. 400M+ commercial 365 seats converting at 10–20% to Copilot Premium at $30/month = 2.5x revenue per seat vs. base tier. Azure AI workloads are sticky: switching cost is 12–24 months. Each Fortune 500 company's AI pipeline runs on Azure fine-tuning with OpenAI exclusivity — the competitive moat for enterprise AI infrastructure is 3–5 years of switching friction.
ideas.driver: Copilot monetization at scale — 400M+ 365 commercial seats with 10–20% penetration to Copilot Premium; Azure AI revenue compounding at 35%+ YoY through FY27; GitHub Copilot Enterprise expansion (software dev workflow AI becoming standard); sovereign AI infrastructure licensing (EU, Middle East)
ideas.risk: OpenAI explores independent cloud or direct enterprise relationships (partnership deteriorates); Google Gemini captures enterprise AI at a lower price point; FOMC rate hold through 2028 compresses MSFT multiple from current 32x forward to 25x; EU AI Act compliance costs ($2–5B one-time)

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: META has the most direct AI-to-revenue conversion path of any big-tech name. AI ad targeting improvements compound instantaneously: every 1% improvement in CTR translates directly to revenue across 3.3B daily active users without an enterprise sales cycle. LLaMA 4 open-source flywheel creates developer ecosystem moat. AI Reality Labs (AR glasses + AI assistant) is a 2027–2028 option currently priced at near-zero.
ideas.why: 3.3B daily active users is an unassailable data and distribution moat for AI training and deployment. Every new AI feature reaches 3.3B users in real-time — the monetization feedback loop has zero lag. META's Zuckerberg AI personal assistant is the first consumer AI product with genuine distribution at scale. EU AI Act compliance is a cost, not an existential risk. META's FCF generation ($60B+ annual) makes it the most rate-resistant large-cap AI name.
ideas.driver: AI ad efficiency compounding — CPM expansion from AI targeting at 3.3B scale; LLaMA 4 ecosystem lock-in monetized through Meta AI products; AR glasses (Ray-Ban Meta) transitioning as AI assistant integration deepens; Q2 2026 earnings (late July) confirming AI monetization at scale in the first full-AI-feature quarter
ideas.risk: Apple iOS ATT 3.0 (hypothetical) restricts cross-app tracking further; EU AI Act creates discriminatory compliance burden; ad recession in H2 2026 if NFP weakness signals broader employment slowdown; AI Reality Labs losses exceed $20B/year, offsetting core FCF

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Bitcoin's April 2024 halving creates the supply shock that historically precedes a 12–18 month bull cycle peak. Post-halving cycle target: $90,000–$120,000 by mid-2027. IBIT institutionalized spot demand — daily net flows now drive price more than miner selling. The current $58,647 price on Day 11 of the exit gate sequence is a tactical drawdown within an intact structural bull cycle. CONVICTION maintained at MEDIUM despite the $58,100 intraday breach today ($57,802 low): the structural thesis is unchanged; the tactical posture is flat/cash until two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000 AND IBIT inflows resume.
ideas.why: Halving math: miner revenue dropped 50%, forcing weakest miners offline and permanently removing ~450 BTC/day of daily sell pressure. IBIT institutionalized demand that didn't exist in prior halvings. US crypto regulatory clarity (2026 SEC under new leadership) legitimizing the asset class. At $58,647 in Extreme Fear with a post-halving supply shock and US equity regime clearing (SPX touching 7,494 today), the medium-term risk/reward is asymmetric. Record June IBIT outflows ($4.5B) are a leading indicator for the subsequent re-accumulation cycle.
ideas.driver: Post-halving supply shock fully pricing in through Q3–Q4 2026; IBIT inflow resumption post-NFP resolution (institutional BTC re-allocation after Q2 uncertainty clears); US crypto regulatory clarity (SEC formalization of spot ETF framework for ETH and SOL); El Salvador, Bhutan, UAE sovereign adoption expanding the global institutional base
ideas.risk: US Congress adverse crypto legislation (unfavorable tax treatment or leverage restrictions); IBIT sustained outflows for 10+ consecutive days (11 so far — watch the turning point); Mt. Gox trustee distribution residual claims creating second supply overhang wave; BTC closes UTC below $58,100 tonight confirming structural support failure (next target $57,500)

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.timeframe: 3–12 months (through Nasdaq 100 inclusion, earnings, and SpaceX IPO optionality)
ideas.idea: SPCX carries the most binary structural optionality in the portfolio. The step-aside tactical posture (bond distribution Day 7, clearance est. July 9–11, re-entry gate $185) is unchanged. But the long-term thesis is the same: September 2 first earnings (Starlink ARR, Starship revenue, Cursor AI) is the fundamental anchoring event; the $148–$170 accumulation window may be the 2026 entry zone; and a SpaceX IPO (rumored 2026–2027) would make SPCX the primary liquid retail vehicle for SpaceX exposure.
ideas.why: Space infrastructure is at the same inflection point cloud computing crossed in 2012–2014: cost curves have collapsed (Falcon 9 reuse 250+ flights, Starship development) but revenue generation is in its first commercial innings. Starlink is profitable. SpaceX DoD backlog is $10B+. At $170.86, SPCX is at a level consistent with the $148–$170 base accumulation window before the September 2 fundamental anchor event. Nasdaq 100 inclusion July 7 ($4.3B passive) is the near-term systematic driver.
ideas.driver: Nasdaq 100 inclusion July 7 (~$4.3B systematic inflows from QQQ/QQQM); SpaceX IPO optionality (2026–2027 rumored) creating retail demand for the only public SpaceX vehicle; September 2 first post-IPO earnings (Starlink ARR, Starship revenue recognition, Cursor AI $500M+ threshold); Starlink terminal adoption acceleration in emerging markets and DoD Starshield contracts
ideas.risk: December 9 lock-up expiry (180 days from June 12 IPO) — float expands from ~4% to 9–14%, creating structural supply ceiling before September 2 earnings anchor; SpaceX IPO delayed to 2028+ removing the primary SPCX optionality catalyst; Nasdaq 100 inclusion demand fully absorbed before re-entry gate activates; bond distribution second wave above $165 pushing back $185 gate timeline
